mainTopic: Whether ״מִשְׁרַת״ teaches היתר מצטרף לאיסור or טעם כעיקר, and where each side learns the other rule.
overview: אביי presses רב דימי: if permitted food joins forbidden food (היתר מצטרף לאיסור), a case where the חולין is the majority makes sense, but under רב דימי's reason (כזית בכדי אכילת פרס) it should make no difference. רב דימי answers that תרומה nowadays is only דרבנן, so it proves nothing. אביי then suggests that ״מִשְׁרַת״ might teach טעם כעיקר instead. He brings a ברייתא that reads it that way and extends the rule to all prohibitions by a קל וחומר from נזיר to כלאי הכרם and ערלה. A scholar answers that רבי אבהו's teaching follows רבי עקיבא. The גמרא finds the right source for this: not the משנה, which is unclear, but a ברייתא where a כזית of bread and wine together makes a נזיר liable. The גמרא then asks where רבי עקיבא learns טעם כעיקר, and answers that he learns it from בשר בחלב. The רבנן reject that source because בשר בחלב is a חידוש: soaking meat in milk is permitted, but cooking it is forbidden. Since רבי עקיבא must also agree it is a חידוש, the גמרא begins a new answer for him that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: אביי: Your explanation can't handle a majority of non-sacred dough
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues that his own reason (היתר מצטרף לאיסור) fits a case where the חולין is the majority. רב דימי's reason (כזית בכדי אכילת פרס) does not fit it, because a majority of חולין changes nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי says: My view works. I hold the reason is that permitted food joins with forbidden food, and I can say the case is one where the חולין is the majority. But you say the reason is that a כזית is eaten within the time of אכילת פרס. Then even if the חולין is the majority, what difference does that make?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי continues his argument with רב דימי. He shows that a majority of חולין matters under his own explanation but makes no difference under רב דימי's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רב דימי's reason, the only question is whether a כזית of the forbidden food is eaten within the time of אכילת פרס. The amount of permitted food around it shouldn't matter. אביי says a detail like 'the חולין is the majority' only makes sense if permitted and forbidden food are joining together, which is his view.

keyTerms.meaning: Permitted food joins with forbidden food to make up the required amount
An olive-sized amount eaten within the time it takes to eat half a loaf
Ordinary, non-sacred food
Granted; it works out well (sets up a contrast)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two reasons. אביי's reason is about permitted food joining forbidden food. רב דימי's reason is about how much forbidden food is eaten within a set amount of time, and the permitted food plays no part.

phrases.english: Granted, according to me, as I say
that it is because permitted food combines with forbidden food,
[I can say the case is] for example where the non-sacred food is more.
But according to you, who say
that it is because there is an olive-bulk
within the time it takes to eat a half-loaf
if the non-sacred food is more, what of it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues אביי's series of objections to רב דימי from the earlier part of the sugya.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב דימי's explanation that the case is about כזית בכדי אכילת פרס
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under רב דימי's reason, a majority of חולין is irrelevant, so the case cannot be explained by it. Under אביי's reason, it fits.

steps.title: רב דימי: תרומה nowadays is only rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי answers that the case is about תרומה in our times, which is only דרבנן, so it is treated more leniently.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Leave aside תרומה nowadays, which is only rabbinic.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי answers אביי. The lenient ruling in this case can't prove anything about Torah law, because תרומה today is only a rabbinic rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב דימי does not argue that a majority of חולין matters under his reason. He sidesteps the proof instead: since תרומה nowadays is only דרבנן, the חכמים could be lenient there. The case therefore tells us nothing about real Torah-level rules.

keyTerms.meaning: Leave it aside; set it apart
תרומה in our times (after the exile)
Of rabbinic (not Torah) law

phrases.english: He said to him: Leave aside תרומה
phrases.notes: רב דימי is the one speaking here, answering אביי.

phrases.english: in the present time, which is rabbinic.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הַנַּח לִתְרוּמָה בַּזְּמַן הַזֶּה דְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the source: the case is rabbinic, so it can't teach Torah law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The lenient case with a majority of חולין proves that היתר מצטרף לאיסור is the reason.
steps.terutzMaskana: The leniency comes from תרומה nowadays being only דרבנן, so it proves nothing.

steps.title: אביי: Maybe ״מִשְׁרַת״ teaches that taste counts like substance
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks how we know that ״מִשְׁרַת״ teaches היתר מצטרף לאיסור. It might instead teach טעם כעיקר.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: How do you know that this word 'soaked' comes to teach that permitted food joins with forbidden food? Maybe it comes to teach that taste is like the substance itself!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי now goes after the source itself. He asks whether the word ״מִשְׁרַת״ might be teaching a completely different rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now, everyone assumed ״מִשְׁרַת״ was the source for היתר מצטרף לאיסור. אביי suggests it could be the source for טעם כעיקר instead: food that absorbed the taste of something forbidden takes on that forbidden status. If so, the whole basis for רב דימי's teaching is shaken.

keyTerms.meaning: Soaking; the word in the נזיר's verse about grapes
The taste of a forbidden food counts like the food itself
From where? How do you know?
Perhaps

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
From where do you know that this word 'soaked'
comes to teach that permitted food combines with forbidden food?

phrases.aramaic: דִּילְמָא לִיתֵּן טַעַם כְּעִיקָּר הוּא דַּאֲתָא!
phrases.english: Perhaps it comes to establish that taste is like the substance!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִמַּאי דְּהַאי ״מִשְׁרַת״ לְהֶיתֵּר מִצְטָרֵף לְאִיסּוּר הוּא דַּאֲתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the argument about the case ends, אביי questions the verse that the whole discussion rests on.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of ״מִשְׁרַת״ as a source for היתר מצטרף לאיסור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word could just as easily teach טעם כעיקר, so it may not prove היתר מצטרף לאיסור at all.

steps.title: The גמרא is surprised that אביי switched sides
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא wonders why אביי, who first argued that היתר מצטרף לאיסור applies everywhere, now suggests the verse teaches טעם כעיקר instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to אביי: At first, what רב דימי said was difficult for him, and he raised all these objections against him. Then he turns around and says to him that the verse teaches that taste is like the substance?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא steps in with surprise at אביי's own behavior. His new question seems to contradict everything he argued before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב דימי limited היתר מצטרף לאיסור to נזיר. אביי objected again and again, trying to show it applies everywhere. Now אביי suggests ״מִשְׁרַת״ might not teach היתר מצטרף לאיסור at all, which seems to undercut his own earlier position.

keyTerms.meaning: At first; originally
He objects; raises a challenge
Objections; refutations
He then turned around; again

phrases.english: And according to Abaye, at first it was difficult for him
what רב דימי said,
phrases.notes: This refers to רב דימי's report that permitted food joins forbidden food only for a נזיר.

phrases.aramaic: וְקָא מוֹתֵיב לֵיהּ כׇּל הָלֵין תְּיוּבָתָא.
phrases.english: and he raised against him all these objections.

phrases.aramaic: הֲדַר אֲמַר לֵיהּ, לִיתֵּן טַעַם כְּעִיקָּר?
phrases.english: Then he turned and said to him that it comes to establish that taste is like substance?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְאַבָּיֵי, מֵעִיקָּרָא קָא קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ מַאי דְּקָאָמַר רַב דִּימִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to אביי's question in step 3 by pointing out that it seems to conflict with his earlier objections.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's suggestion in step 3 that ״מִשְׁרַת״ teaches טעם כעיקר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אביי earlier fought to show that היתר מצטרף לאיסור applies everywhere. Now he seems to deny that the verse teaches it at all, which looks like a contradiction.

steps.title: אביי spoke only after רב דימי had answered him
steps.stepSummary: אביי's suggestion came after he had already accepted רב דימי's answer, so it does not contradict his earlier position.
steps.simpleTranslation: After רב דימי answered him, אביי said to him: Maybe the word ״מִשְׁרַת״ comes to teach that the taste of a forbidden food is like its substance?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the timing. אביי said ״מִשְׁרַת״ might teach טעם כעיקר only after רב דימי had already answered his objections.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 4 it looked strange that אביי would treat היתר מצטרף לאיסור as a rule everywhere and then suggest a different meaning for the verse. The answer is that he had changed his position. Once רב דימי showed that היתר מצטרף לאיסור is not a rule for all Torah prohibitions, אביי was free to propose that the verse teaches טעם כעיקר instead.

keyTerms.meaning: After he answered him
The taste of a forbidden food counts like the food itself
Perhaps, maybe
"Soaking": the word in the פסוק about a נזיר

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not contradicting himself. He made the two claims at different times: first before רב דימי answered him, and then after.

phrases.english: After he had answered him,
phrases.notes: This means after רב דימי's answer in step 2, which אביי accepted.

phrases.english: he said to him:
perhaps to establish that taste is like the substance
is what it comes for?
phrases.notes: "It" is the word ״מִשְׁרַת״ in the פסוק.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4 by explaining when אביי made each claim.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Timing: the two claims were made at different stages of the conversation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אביי contradicts himself by holding that היתר מצטרף לאיסור applies everywhere while reading the verse as teaching טעם כעיקר.
steps.terutzMaskana: אביי made his suggestion only after accepting רב דימי's answer, so there is no contradiction.

steps.title: The ברייתא: ״מִשְׁרַת״ teaches that taste counts like substance
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from ״מִשְׁרַת״ that a נזיר is liable for water that tastes like wine, and extends this to all Torah prohibitions.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught in a ברייתא: ״מִשְׁרַת״ teaches that taste is like substance. If a נזיר soaked grapes in water and the water tastes like wine, he is liable. From here you learn the same for all prohibitions of the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a ברייתא that reads ״מִשְׁרַת״ exactly the way he suggested, as the source for טעם כעיקר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The water contains no actual wine, only its taste, yet the נזיר is liable as if he drank wine. That shows taste alone counts. The ברייתא then says this rule is not limited to נזיר but is the model for every Torah prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: It is taught in a ברייתא
He soaked
Liable to punishment
You learn, you derive

steps.whyThisMatters: If ״מִשְׁרַת״ is used for טעם כעיקר, it is no longer available to teach היתר מצטרף לאיסור. That creates a problem for רבי יוחנן's reading of the word, which step 9 answers.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא:
"Soaking" is to establish that taste is like substance,
that if he soaked grapes in water
and they have the taste of wine
he is liable.
And from here you derive
all the prohibitions in the Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the ברייתא source behind אביי's suggested reading of ״מִשְׁרַת״.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ״מִשְׁרַת״ teaches טעם כעיקר. A נזיר who drinks water that tastes like wine is liable, and the same rule applies to all Torah prohibitions.

steps.title: The קל וחומר from נזיר to כלאי הכרם
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא proves that the rule spreads to other prohibitions: if the lighter prohibition of נזיר has טעם כעיקר, then the stricter כלאי הכרם surely does.
steps.simpleTranslation: A נזיר's prohibition is not permanent, is not a ban on benefit, and can be released, yet the Torah made taste like substance for him. כלאי הכרם is permanent, is a ban on benefit, and cannot be released. Isn't it logical that taste counts like substance there too?!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains how it extends טעם כעיקר from נזיר to other prohibitions. It uses a קל וחומר, starting with כלאי הכרם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists three ways the נזיר prohibition is lighter: it is temporary, it allows benefit, and the vow can be undone. כלאי הכרם is stricter in all three ways. So if even the lighter case has טעם כעיקר, the stricter case certainly does.

keyTerms.meaning: A permanent prohibition
A ban on any benefit, not just eating
A way to undo the prohibition
Forbidden mixed planting in a vineyard
Is it not logical? (the language of a קל וחומר)

phrases.english: And just as a נזיר,
whose prohibition is not a permanent prohibition,
and whose prohibition is not a ban on benefit,
and there is a release for his prohibition
phrases.notes: He can go to a חכם and have his vow undone.

phrases.english: for him [the Torah] made taste like substance.
Mixed seeds of the vineyard,
whose prohibition is a permanent prohibition,
and whose prohibition is a ban on benefit,
and there is no release for their prohibition

phrases.aramaic: — אֵינוֹ דִּין שֶׁיַּעֲשֶׂה בּוֹ טַעַם כְּעִיקָּר?!
phrases.english: is it not logical that it should make taste like substance for it?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמָה נָזִיר שֶׁאֵין אִיסּוּרוֹ אִיסּוּר עוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the ברייתא of step 6 extends the rule from נזיר to all Torah prohibitions.
steps.raayaObject: That טעם כעיקר applies to כלאי הכרם and other prohibitions.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from נזיר, whose prohibition is lighter in three ways.

steps.title: The same reasoning works for ערלה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds that ערלה also has טעם כעיקר, because it is stricter than נזיר in two of the three ways.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the same is true for ערלה, on two of the three counts.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends by applying the same קל וחומר to ערלה, even though ערלה is stricter than נזיר in only two ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ערלה is not permanent, since the tree's later fruit is allowed. But it is a ban on benefit and cannot be released. Being stricter than נזיר in those two ways is enough for the קל וחומר to work.

keyTerms.meaning: Fruit from a tree's first three years, which is forbidden
And the same law applies
On two (of the three counts)

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא reads ״מִשְׁרַת״ as the source for טעם כעיקר. It extends this from נזיר to the rest of the Torah: נזיר is a light prohibition, so stricter ones like כלאי הכרם and ערלה surely follow the same rule.

phrases.english: And the same is true for ערלה
on two counts.
phrases.notes: ערלה is a ban on benefit and can't be released, but it isn't permanent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the קל וחומר of step 7 to ערלה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: טעם כעיקר applies to ערלה, since it is stricter than נזיר in two of the three ways.

steps.title: A scholar says רבי אבהו follows רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: One of the רבנן tells אביי that רבי אבהו's teaching (היתר מצטרף לאיסור from ״מִשְׁרַת״) follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: One of the Sages said to אביי: When רבי אבהו said that rule, he said it according to רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: A scholar tells אביי that רבי אבהו's rule matches the view of רבי עקיבא. This sets up the next question: which teaching of רבי עקיבא does he mean?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא in steps 6-8 used ״מִשְׁרַת״ for טעם כעיקר, which seems to leave no room for רבי יוחנן's reading of it as היתר מצטרף לאיסור. The scholar answers that רבי אבהו, quoting רבי יוחנן, follows רבי עקיבא, a תנא who reads the word differently from that ברייתא. The ברייתא is then just the other side of a disagreement between תנאים.

keyTerms.meaning: One of the Sages (an unnamed scholar)
The אמורא who taught היתר מצטרף לאיסור in the name of רבי יוחנן
When he said it

phrases.english: One of the Sages said to him:
When Rabbi Abbahu said it,
he was saying it according to Rabbi Akiva.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty from the ברייתא in steps 6-8. רבי אבהו's derivation of היתר מצטרף לאיסור from ״מִשְׁרַת״ follows רבי עקיבא, who disagrees with that ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אבהו's rule of היתר מצטרף לאיסור follows the opinion of רבי עקיבא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns the disputed reading to a specific תנא (רבי עקיבא) who disagrees with the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's reading of ״מִשְׁרַת״ as טעם כעיקר contradicts רבי יוחנן's reading of it as היתר מצטרף לאיסור.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוחנן's reading follows רבי עקיבא, who disagrees with that ברייתא.

steps.title: Which teaching of רבי עקיבא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which statement of רבי עקיבא is being referred to.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which רבי עקיבא do you mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which teaching of רבי עקיבא shows that he holds היתר מצטרף לאיסור. This question sets up a search through his sources.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying a rule "follows רבי עקיבא" only works if we can point to a real source. The גמרא now wants that source.

keyTerms.meaning: Which?

phrases.english: Which Rabbi Akiva?
phrases.notes: He means: which statement of רבי עקיבא?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind the attribution in step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which statement of רבי עקיבא shows that he holds היתר מצטרף לאיסור.

steps.title: First suggestion: רבי עקיבא in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the source is the משנה where רבי עקיבא says a נזיר who soaked bread in wine is liable if there is enough to make a כזית.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we say it is רבי עקיבא of our משנה: we learned that רבי עקיבא says that even if a נזיר soaked his bread in wine, and there is enough to combine into a כזית, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a first answer: the משנה where רבי עקיבא speaks about bread soaked in wine. This is only a suggestion, and the next step will test it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words "enough to combine into a כזית" sound like the bread and wine join together to make the amount. If so, the permitted bread is adding to the forbidden wine, which is היתר מצטרף לאיסור.

keyTerms.meaning: If we say (opens a suggestion that may be rejected)
He soaked his bread in wine
To combine
An olive-bulk, the minimum amount for liability

phrases.english: If we say it is Rabbi Akiva of here,
phrases.notes: "Of here" means the משנה in our own פרק.

phrases.english: as we learned in a mishna: Rabbi Akiva says:
Even if he soaked his bread in wine
and there is enough in it to combine into an olive-bulk,
he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first answer to the question in step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A tentative answer: the source is רבי עקיבא's statement in the משנה about bread soaked in wine.

steps.title: Maybe the משנה means a full כזית of wine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: the משנה might mean there is a full כזית of wine by itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: But how do you know? Maybe he means that there is a כזית of wine as it is, by itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the suggestion. The משנה could simply mean the wine alone adds up to a כזית, with no help from the bread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the wine alone is a כזית, the bread adds nothing, and there is no proof for היתר מצטרף לאיסור. The משנה's words are open to both readings, so they cannot serve as a clear source.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do you know?
Perhaps
As is, in its own form

phrases.english: But from where do you know? Perhaps
it is only when there is an olive-bulk as is!
phrases.notes: "As is" means enough wine by itself, without counting the bread.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִמַּאי? דִּילְמָא הוּא דְּאִיכָּא כְּזַיִת בָּעֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof offered in step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the משנה as a source for רבי עקיבא holding היתר מצטרף לאיסור.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה can be read as requiring a כזית of wine alone, so the bread may not be joining at all.

steps.title: Then what would רבי עקיבא be adding?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא anticipates a challenge: if the wine alone is a כזית, what new point is רבי עקיבא making?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: what is the point of saying this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא imagines someone objecting to its rejection. If the wine alone is a כזית, a נזיר is obviously liable, so why would רבי עקיבא need to say it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: This challenge tries to rescue the proof. A statement in a משנה should teach something new. Reading it as "a full כזית of wine" seems to make it say nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say
What is the point of saying it? (It seems obvious)

phrases.english: And if you will say: what is the point of saying this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rejection in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that רבי עקיבא's משנה requires a full כזית of wine alone.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under that reading the ruling seems obvious, and a משנה should teach something new.

steps.title: The point is to argue with the תנא קמא
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא's point is that a כזית of wine is enough, against the תנא קמא who requires a רביעית.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to exclude the view of the תנא קמא, who said a נזיר is liable only if he drinks a רביעית of wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. רבי עקיבא is teaching the amount: a כזית of wine makes a נזיר liable, not the larger רביעית that the תנא קמא requires.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the statement has a clear new point, there is no need to read it as bread joining wine. The rejection from step 12 stands, and the משנה is not a proof.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude, to argue against
The first, unnamed opinion in a משנה
A quarter-לוג, a larger measure of liquid

phrases.english: It is to exclude the view of the first tanna,
who said: not until he drinks a quarter-log of wine!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 13 and keeps the rejection of step 12 in place.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the statement a new point (the amount), so the bread-joining reading is not needed.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without the bread-joining reading, רבי עקיבא's statement would teach nothing new.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי עקיבא is teaching that a כזית, not a רביעית, makes a נזיר liable. So the משנה is no proof.

steps.title: The source is רבי עקיבא in a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The real source is a ברייתא: a נזיר who ate a כזית made of bread and wine together is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is רבי עקיבא of the ברייתא. As it is taught: רבי עקיבא says, a נזיר who soaked his bread in wine and ate a כזית from bread and wine is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final answer to "which רבי עקיבא?" It points to a ברייתא that clearly says the כזית comes from the bread and the wine together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the words "from bread and from wine" leave no room for doubt. The permitted bread joins the forbidden wine to make the כזית. That is exactly היתר מצטרף לאיסור.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (drops the earlier suggestion)
A teaching of the תנאים not included in the משנה
From bread and from wine, together

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא's source for היתר מצטרף לאיסור is the ברייתא, which says outright that the כזית is made of bread and wine together. The משנה is too unclear to prove it.

phrases.english: Rather, it is Rabbi Akiva of the baraita.
As it is taught: Rabbi Akiva says:
A nazirite who soaked his bread in wine
and ate an olive-bulk from the bread and wine is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected משנה with a clear ברייתא as the answer to step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is the ברייתא where רבי עקיבא makes a נזיר liable for a כזית made of bread and wine together.

steps.title: Where does רבי עקיבא learn טעם כעיקר?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרב אויא asks רב אשי: since רבי עקיבא uses ״מִשְׁרַת״ for היתר מצטרף לאיסור, what is his source for טעם כעיקר?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בריה דרב אויא said to רב אשי: רבי עקיבא uses the verse ״וְכׇל מִשְׁרַת״ for היתר מצטרף לאיסור. So from where does he learn טעם כעיקר?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question opens. The ברייתא in step 6 learned טעם כעיקר from ״מִשְׁרַת״, but רבי עקיבא uses that verse for a different rule. So where does he get טעם כעיקר?
steps.deeperAnalysis: One verse is normally used for one teaching. If רבי עקיבא uses ״מִשְׁרַת״ for היתר מצטרף לאיסור, it is "used up" for him, and he needs another source for טעם כעיקר.

keyTerms.meaning: He applies (the verse) to
"Anything soaked": the verse about a נזיר and grape-soaked liquid
Permitted food combines with forbidden food to make up the amount
The taste of a forbidden food counts like the food itself
From where does he learn it?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אַוְיָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Aḥa, son of Rav Avya, said to Rav Ashi:
According to Rabbi Akiva, who applies
this verse, "anything soaked,"
to the rule that permitted combines with forbidden,
from where does he learn to treat taste like the substance itself?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 15. Since רבי עקיבא uses the verse for היתר מצטרף לאיסור, it asks for his source for טעם כעיקר.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's source for טעם כעיקר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse ״מִשְׁרַת״ is already used for היתר מצטרף לאיסור, so it cannot also teach טעם כעיקר for him.

steps.title: He learns טעם כעיקר from בשר בחלב
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא learns טעם כעיקר from בשר בחלב, where only the taste of the milk is in the meat and it is still forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from meat and milk. Is it not just taste there, and it is forbidden? Here too, it is no different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי עקיבא learns טעם כעיקר from בשר בחלב. Cooked meat holds only the taste of the milk, yet the Torah forbids it, so taste counts for other prohibitions too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In בשר בחלב no actual milk is left in the meat, only its absorbed taste, and the Torah still forbids it. That shows taste alone can make food forbidden. רבי עקיבא applies this to all איסורים, so he does not need ״מִשְׁרַת״ for טעם כעיקר.

keyTerms.meaning: He learns (it from another case)
Meat cooked in milk
Merely taste
It is no different

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי עקיבא, ״מִשְׁרַת״ teaches היתר מצטרף לאיסור, and טעם כעיקר comes from בשר בחלב, where taste alone is forbidden.

phrases.english: He learns it from meat cooked in milk.
Is it not merely taste there, and yet it is forbidden?
phrases.notes: Once the meat is cooked, only the milk's taste is in it, not the milk itself.

phrases.english: Here too, it is no different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16 by giving another source for טעם כעיקר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a different source: learning by comparison from בשר בחלב.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without ״מִשְׁרַת״, רבי עקיבא would seem to have no source for טעם כעיקר.
steps.terutzMaskana: בשר בחלב shows that taste alone can be forbidden. The same applies to other איסורים.

steps.title: The Rabbis do not learn from meat and milk because it is a one-of-a-kind law
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן do not learn טעם כעיקר from בשר בחלב, because בשר בחלב is a חידוש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the Rabbis? They say we do not learn from meat and milk, because it is a one-of-a-kind law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the רבנן do not learn טעם כעיקר from בשר בחלב the way רבי עקיבא does. It answers that בשר בחלב is a חידוש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 17, רבי עקיבא learned טעם כעיקר from בשר בחלב. The רבנן have their own source, ״מִשְׁרַת״. Here the גמרא explains that they reject the בשר בחלב source, because you cannot build a general rule from a law that is unusual.

keyTerms.meaning: A novel, one-of-a-kind law that does not follow normal logic
We learn or derive (a rule from a source)
The Rabbis who disagree with רבי עקיבא and learn טעם כעיקר from ״מִשְׁרַת״

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic rule of learning: you do not build a general principle on a חידוש.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis: we do not learn from meat and milk,
because it is a novelty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the רבנן reject the source רבי עקיבא used in step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Disqualifying the source as a חידוש
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everyone should learn טעם כעיקר from בשר בחלב.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רבנן do not, because בשר בחלב is a חידוש and cannot teach a general rule.

steps.title: What is the novelty? Not 'each alone is fine but together forbidden,' since mixed kinds is the same
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the חידוש of בשר בחלב is. It rejects the idea that the חידוש is 'allowed alone, forbidden together,' because כלאים also works that way.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is its novelty? If you say it is that this alone is permitted and that alone is permitted, but together they are forbidden, then mixed kinds is also like that: this alone is permitted and that alone is permitted, but together they are forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what exactly makes בשר בחלב a חידוש. It tests a first answer and knocks it down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first idea is that meat and milk are each fine alone and forbidden only together. But כלאים has the very same pattern, so this cannot be what makes בשר בחלב unique.

keyTerms.meaning: What is its novelty?
If you say (introduces a suggestion that will be rejected)
Forbidden mixtures of different kinds
Together, with each other

phrases.english: What is its novelty?
If we say that this alone
phrases.notes: "This" is the meat, and "that" in the next row is the milk.

phrases.english: and that alone are permitted,
but together they are forbidden,
mixed kinds also:
this alone is permitted
and that alone is permitted,
but together they are forbidden!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the claim in step 18 that בשר בחלב is a חידוש.
steps.kashyaTarget: The first suggestion: the חידוש is that meat and milk are allowed alone but forbidden together.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: כלאים has the same pattern, so this pattern is not unique and is not a חידוש.

steps.title: The novelty: soaking all day is permitted, but cooking is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The real חידוש of בשר בחלב is that meat soaked in milk all day is permitted, but meat cooked in milk is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the novelty is that if one soaks it all day in milk, it is permitted, but if one cooks it, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the true חידוש of בשר בחלב. Soaking is allowed, but cooking is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Meat soaked in milk all day surely picks up the taste of the milk, yet by Torah law it stays permitted. Only cooking makes it forbidden. Normally the taste alone should forbid it (טעם כעיקר), so this law is unusual, and the רבנן cannot learn a general rule from it.

keyTerms.meaning: Soaks
The whole day
Cooks
Rather (rejects the last idea and brings a new one)

steps.whatToRemember: The חידוש of בשר בחלב is that only cooking forbids it, not soaking, even though soaking also passes on the taste.

phrases.english: Rather: that if one soaks it
all day in milk, it is permitted,
but if one cooks it in cooking, it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: דְּאִי תָּרוּ לֵיהּ כּוּלֵּי יוֹמָא בַּחֲלָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected suggestion in step 19 with a better explanation of the חידוש.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חידוש is 'allowed alone, forbidden together.'
steps.terutzMaskana: The חידוש is that soaking is permitted and only cooking forbids.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא should also agree that meat and milk is a novelty
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי עקיבא can learn טעם כעיקר from בשר בחלב, since he too must agree it is a חידוש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי עקיבא too, isn't meat and milk a novelty?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the question around on רבי עקיבא. If בשר בחלב is a חידוש, how can he learn from it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חידוש from step 20 is a plain fact about the law, so רבי עקיבא cannot deny it. This puts his source from step 17 in danger.

keyTerms.meaning: Also, too

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva too,
isn't meat and milk a novelty?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא נָמֵי, בָּשָׂר בְּחָלָב חִידּוּשׁ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the חידוש from step 20 to challenge רבי עקיבא's source in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's learning of טעם כעיקר from בשר בחלב (step 17).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A חידוש cannot teach a general rule, and בשר בחלב is a חידוש for everyone.

steps.title: Opening a new answer for רבי עקיבא's source
steps.stepSummary: The word אלא signals that the גמרא is about to give a new source for רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather,
steps.whatsHappening: This one word is a setup. The גמרא is dropping the בשר בחלב source and getting ready to give רבי עקיבא a different source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the challenge in step 21 stands, the גמרא gives up on בשר בחלב as רבי עקיבא's source. The new source comes right after this.

phrases.english: Rather,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge of step 21 and begins a new answer.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי עקיבא learns טעם כעיקר from בשר בחלב.
steps.terutzMaskana: A different source will be given for רבי עקיבא.
